facts.statement: Earlier research indicates that groups of neurons in the hippocampus can connect different memories of a place over periods ranging from five hours to seven days.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: This study looked at how memories of neutral and unpleasant situations connect over longer periods and checked which neurons fire again when those memories are recalled.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: The connection between the two types of memories was seen when they were separated by hours, days, or weeks, but not when the gap was extremely short or extremely long.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: Memories that were linked had more neurons firing in both the hippocampus and the amygdala, but this extra overlap was not statistically different from what would be expected by chance.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: When linked memories were recalled, more neurons became active in the CA1 region of the hippocampus and in the lateral and basolateral parts of the amygdala.
facts.subject: animals
